conceptual assets.information: The configuration of each protected region, including its read, write and execute permissions, address mode and address bounds, determines which processor accesses are permitted. The configuration is held in the PMP registers and can be returned through the CSR readback port.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: CSR write data changes the permission and mode fields at lines 129-140 and the region addresses at lines 173-176, so an unauthorized write can alter the protection policy. Availability: the configuration determines allow at lines 323-339 and propagates through fail and fault_o at lines 354-363, so restrictive settings can block required accesses. Undermined Expected Behavior: processor privilege changes the selected permission at lines 321-339 and debug mode suppresses the resulting fault at line 363, allowing the intended protection behavior to be bypassed.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write permissive or restrictive PMP permissions and bounds through the CSR interface to allow an unauthorized access or fault normal accesses.

conceptual assets.information: The lock bit for each PMP region controls whether that region's configuration and address can be changed by later CSR writes. It is retained in the PMP configuration and is visible in CSR readback.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: the lock bit is written from CSR data at line 145 and is then used to prevent configuration writes at lines 127 and 170, so an attacker can set it prematurely and change the protection lifecycle. Availability: the lock condition can reject subsequent writes to the PMP configuration and address registers at lines 127 and 170, withholding required configuration transfers.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could set a region's lock bit before the intended policy is installed, preventing later updates and leaving the system with an unsafe or unusable protection policy.

conceptual assets.information: The effective address selected for the current instruction fetch or load/store is the address against which PMP regions are checked. It has no exit port because the unit consumes it in comparisons; only the resulting permission status leaves the unit.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: the unit selects addr_ls_i or ctrl_i.pc_nxt into acc_addr at line 244 and uses that value in the region comparisons at lines 285 and 295-296, so changing the effective address changes which protection policy is applied. Availability: an altered address can select a denied region and propagate to fail and fault_o through lines 354 and 363, blocking the required access.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could steer the effective address selection so that an access is checked against the wrong region, either bypassing protection or causing normal execution to fault.

conceptual assets.information: The verdict indicates whether the current fetch, load or store is allowed by the PMP configuration and access context, and is returned as the registered fault status. Processor operation depends on this decision to detect denied accesses.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity: the per-region permission and match results combine into fail at lines 351-354 and are registered into fault_o at line 363, so altered policy or access context can change the security verdict. Availability: fault_o is asserted from the denial result at line 363, allowing a denied verdict to stop a required processor access. Undermined Expected Behavior: ctrl_i.cpu_debug masks fail when fault_o is assigned at line 363, so debug mode can suppress a protection fault that should be reported.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could manipulate the protection inputs or debug bypass so that a forbidden access is accepted or a permitted access is reported as a fault.
